ps140: O blessed martyr Eutyches,* having been taught the word of God in sacred manner by the honoured disciple,* the preacher of divine eloquence,* you learned from him every sacred doctrine, and were shown to be a light,* illumining every thought with grace through your sacred theology.* Wherefore, we honour your holy memory.

You cast down the fortress of delusion, O you  who are most rich,* by your steadfast struggle of endurance,* by your wounds and stripes and your glorious death.* Wherefore, you have received immortality,* making your abode with the choirs of the martyrs* and with the ranks of the angels,* being well and perfectly deified in godly manner* by a higher communion.

Imprisoned in a dungeon,* you received the Bread of life from heaven, O glorious one;* and, cast into the flame, you remained unconsumed.* Lacerated with wounds cruelly inflicted,* you tamed the raging of the wild beasts by your prayers.* By the sword was your head severed,* and you were drawn up to the heavens,* as on a divine chariot.
theotokion: Save me, O all-pure Mistress,* who ineffably gave birth to Christ the Saviour;* for you alone have I acquired as our intercessor,* an invincible rampart, protection and joy, and the divine consolation of my soul.* Wherefore, deliver me from the worm which sleeps not* and from the everlasting fire, O Mother of Christ God.
stavrotheotokion: “What is this sight which my eyes behold, O Master?* You who sustain all creation, being lifted up on the Tree and dying, granting life to all!”* said the Theotokos weeping, when she beheld uplifted on the Cross* the God and man who ineffably had shone forth from her.
